question_text:
Name the type of quadrilateral formed, if any, by the following points, and give reasons for your answer:
(i) (- 1, - 2), (1, 0), (- 1, 2), (- 3, 0)
(ii) (- 3, 5), (3, 1), (0, 3), (- 1, - 4)
(iii) (4, 5), (7, 6), (4, 3), (1, 2)

parts.part_text: Let the points ( - 1, - 2), (1, 0), ( - 1, 2), and ( - 3, 0) be representing the vertices A, B, C, and D of the given quadrilateral respectively. It can be observed that all sides of this quadrilateral are of the same length and also, the diagonals are of the same length. Therefore, the given points are the vertices of a square.
parts.answer_text: The quadrilateral formed is a square.

steps.description: Identify the vertices of the quadrilateral and calculate the lengths of the sides and diagonals.
Conclude that all sides and diagonals are equal, confirming it is a square.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, the quadrilateral formed by the points is a square.

parts.part_text: Let the points ( - 3, 5), (3, 1), (0, 3), and ( - 1, - 4) be representing the vertices A, B, C, and D of the given quadrilateral respectively. It can be observed that all sides of this quadrilateral are of different lengths. Therefore, it can be said that it is only a general quadrilateral, and not specific such as square, rectangle, etc.
parts.answer_text: The quadrilateral formed is a general quadrilateral.

steps.description: Identify the vertices of the quadrilateral and calculate the lengths of the sides.
Conclude that the sides are of different lengths, confirming it is a general quadrilateral.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, the quadrilateral formed by the points is a general quadrilateral.

parts.part_text: Let the points (4, 5), (7, 6), (4, 3), and (1, 2) be representing the vertices A, B, C, and D of the given quadrilateral respectively. It can be observed that opposite sides of this quadrilateral are of the same length. However, the diagonals are of different lengths. Therefore, the given points are the vertices of a parallelogram.
parts.answer_text: The quadrilateral formed is a parallelogram.

steps.description: Identify the vertices of the quadrilateral and calculate the lengths of the opposite sides.
Conclude that opposite sides are equal and diagonals are not, confirming it is a parallelogram.

parts.final_answer: Therefore, the quadrilateral formed by the points is a parallelogram.
